property_summary: Call getFirstWithdrawalBonus for an address; the reference contract correctly sends 100 wei to the recipient and sets claimedBonus[recipient]=true, while the buggy version reverts on the external call because it removed the require(success) check but does not revert properly — actually the buggy version fails to revert on a failed call. Since any address will succeed, we test with an externally-owned account (EOA) that accepts ether; the divergence is that the reference sends exactly 100 wei to the recipient (address(this).balance decreases by 100), while the buggy version does not send the ether because the call is not properly handled (the function does not revert but the transfer never happens — actually the buggy version compiles but the call will succeed, but the key issue is the missing `require(success)` — but since all calls to an EOA succeed, both will succeed. We need a scenario where the call would fail: e.g. calling getFirstWithdrawalBonus on itself (the contract itself) which has no receive function. In the reference, withdrawReward is called, which tries to send ether to the contract address (which has no receive), causing revert; thus getFirstWithdrawalBonus reverts. In the buggy version, withdrawReward does not require success, so it proceeds and sets claimedBonus[recipient]=true, but the ether is not actually sent — the contract still holds the ether. Therefore, after the call, the buggy version's address(this).balance remains higher than the reference (which reverts and leaves it unchanged). We will use c.address as recipient: reference reverts, buggy succeeds and sets claimedBonus. We catch the revert with try/catch and assert that in the reference, getFirstWithdrawalBonus reverts (i.e., ok == false), while in the buggy version it does not revert (ok == true) and claimedBonus is set.
